title: When is it due?
hook: You work on UTC. Your colleague works on UTC+9.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that a time without a time zone is read in each reader's own zone, which can move it by hours

misconception: A date and clock time mean the same moment for every reader.
objective: Replace an ambiguous deadline with an explicit dated time zone.

claims.text: Scenario and prediction: You work on UTC. Your colleague works on UTC+9. Your colleague reads 'Due 16 Oct, 15:00' as their own time. When is that for you? Correct option: 06:00 UTC, 9 h early. Fixture zones and times are stipulated.
claims.source: 15:00 at UTC+9 = 06:00 UTC. Content patch r9 batch D (cm-lifehacks, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/content-patch-r9-batch-d.md block 13), applied by demo-builder for W-608 (2026-10-14).

claims.text: A date, a clock time and a zone fix one moment. Without the zone, a reader on UTC+9 who assumes their own time aims 9 hours early. Daylight-saving rules are outside this exercise.

claims.note: FC W-740 (2026-10-14): Same arithmetic; a zone-less reader on UTC+9 aims 9 h early. DST disclaimer accurate.

claims.text: UTC is one shared reference, so 17:00 UTC is one moment everywhere. 'Local' and 'close of day' each mean a different moment in each city.
claims.source: Recall why; stipulated example. Content patch r9 batch D (cm-lifehacks, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/content-patch-r9-batch-d.md block 13), applied by demo-builder for W-608 (2026-10-14).
claims.note: FC W-740 (2026-10-14): On Fri 16 Oct 2026, London is UTC+1 (BST until 25 Oct) and Tokyo UTC+9 (tzdata 2026e from PyPI wheel and the system zoneinfo): 17:00 local = 16:00Z vs 08:00Z, different moments; 17:00 UTC is one moment.

claims.text: A UTC+9 reader who takes 'Due 16 Oct, 15:00' as local time aims for 06:00 UTC, 9 hours before 15:00 UTC.
claims.source: 15:00 − 9 h = 06:00; consequence field in studyCatalog.ts. Content patch r9 batch D (cm-lifehacks, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/content-patch-r9-batch-d.md block 13), applied by demo-builder for W-608 (2026-10-14).
claims.note: FC W-740 (2026-10-14): 15:00 - 9 h = 06:00 UTC; matches the consequence cell.

claims.source: Any 2026 calendar (needed because the recall says 'Fri 16 Oct'). Content patch r9 batch D (cm-lifehacks, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/content-patch-r9-batch-d.md block 13), applied by demo-builder for W-608 (2026-10-14).
claims.note: FC W-740 (2026-10-14): Friday, by four independent computations: JS Date (UTC), Zeller's congruence, a day count from Sat 1 Jan 2000 (9,785 days, 9785 mod 7 = 6 → Friday), and GNU date / Python datetime. 14 Oct 2026 is a Wednesday, so the patch's fix is right. Derived from the Gregorian calendar, no outside source needed.

claims.text: Seen table and first reveal sentence: No zone: your colleague aims for 06:00 UTC, 9 h early; fields 2/3. With zone: your colleague aims for 15:00 UTC; fields 3/3.

recall.question: Your team works in London and Tokyo. Which deadline means the same moment for both?
recall.why: UTC is one shared reference, so 17:00 UTC is one moment everywhere. 'Local' and 'close of day' each mean a different moment in each city.
